archimate:Principle.name: choreography
archimate:Principle.documentation:
CONTEXT
The Integration Layer Pilot proves three patterns on Azure Integration Services. It is a proof of concept and will not progress to live production. For Choreography, a change in a source system is published as an event to Azure Service Bus, and subscribing applications receive it through independent subscriptions without point-to-point connectivity.
Dynamics 365 (Dataverse) is the operational master for Organisation (account) and Customer (contact) data, and also holds the data for Building (invln_sites). It is the source of truth for the choreography pilot.
PROPOSAL
Publish changes from Dynamics 365 to Azure Service Bus through an integration layer REST API, hosted on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) behind API Management and secured with Entra ID OAuth 2.0.
When an Organisation (account), Building (invln_sites) or Customer (contact) record is created, updated or deactivated in Dynamics 365, an asynchronous trigger calls the AKS publishing API. The API maps the record to the canonical model and publishes it as an event to a Service Bus topic. Subscribers receive events through their own subscriptions.
